$comment: DELIBERATELY PAUSED ESTATES — consumed by scripts/ci/_estate-pause-declaration.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The estate pause/resume mandate keeps the sovereign and
Commercial estates STOPPED unless something is actively being validated. A stopped
ADX cluster cannot take the Microsoft.Kusto/clusters/principalAssignments the
template declares on it, so a deploy lane pointed at a paused estate fails — and it
fails for a reason that is now deliberate.
THE FIX IS NOT 'SKIP WHEN STOPPED'. Intent is not inferable from state: a genuinely
broken cluster and a deliberately stopped one look identical to `az resource show`.
A lane keyed to the STATE would read a real outage as fine forever, on a P0 deploy
path, in a boundary nobody watches closely. This file is the EXPLICIT signal instead,
and it is the only thing that can suppress the failure.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A REPO VARIABLE — the same answer
scripts/ci/workflow-lane-states-allowlist.json gives for workflow disablement: a
repo variable is 'one click, no commit, no review, no record'. This file IS the
record, and it is the same shape as that allowlist on purpose.
RULES (enforced by _estate-pause-declaration.mjs, not by convention). Every one of
them resolves to NOT-PAUSED on failure, so a malformed entry can never silence a
lane by accident — it just stops suppressing, and the script prints which rule it
failed:
1. `boundary` must match CSA_LOOM_BOUNDARY on the lane exactly (GCC-High, GCC,
IL5, Commercial). One boundary's declaration never covers another's.
2. `owner` is required. A paused estate has an owner, not just a note.
3. `reason` must be at least 60 characters and free of TODO/TBD/WIP. State what
was stopped, what was MEASURED, and what must be true to resume. Do not state
a motive you did not establish (.claude/rules/deploy-integrity.md R7).
4. `reviewBy` (YYYY-MM-DD) is required and EXPIRES. Past its date the estate reads
as NOT declared paused, the preflight resumes trying to start the cluster, and
the lane goes red again. Without an expiry a pause is permanent by default,
which is how a lane stays dark for months while every dashboard reads green
(deploy-integrity.md R3). It must be LATER than `declaredOn`.
5. `declaredOn` (YYYY-MM-DD) is required, must not be in the future, and is the
single most load-bearing field here (#4121). A stood-down run SUCCEEDS having
deployed nothing, so scripts/ci/check-deploy-staleness.mjs DISCARDS successful
runs dated on or after `declaredOn` — otherwise a paused lane would report `ok`
while nothing had deployed for months. Two ways it goes inert, both reproduced:
- a FUTURE `declaredOn` keeps every run, so driftDays reads 0 and the check
exits 0. Now refused: a declaration cannot be dated later than the run
reading it.
- RE-DATING IT ON RENEWAL does the same with no mistake at all, which is why
the rule is: `declaredOn` is when the pause BEGAN and is NEVER moved.
6. `renewedOn` (YYYY-MM-DD, optional) is where a renewal records its fresh read.
RENEWING A PAUSE = bump `reviewBy` + set `renewedOn`. Do NOT touch `declaredOn`;
moving it forward re-hides every day of drift that accumulated behind it. It
must not precede `declaredOn` and must not be in the future. Nothing keys the
staleness filter to it, deliberately — the field a renewal touches must not be
the field the filter reads.
WHAT A DECLARATION DOES NOT DO. It does not excuse a cluster in Unavailable,
Deleting, Deleted, or an unrecognised state — those stay red. It does not excuse an
unreadable control plane. And it does not make the lane report success: a paused
run SKIPS the what-if and the apply and says so, which is UNMEASURED, not clean.

paused.reason: The GCC-High estate is held stopped under the estate pause/resume mandate, and the operator has decided the ADX cluster stays stopped rather than being started for each daily run. RENEWED 2026-09-07 after a fresh read; the original reason is superseded because the state it described is no longer the state that is observed. MEASURED at run 33519232492 (2026-09-01, the only run approved past the gcc-high-deploy environment gate since this entry was declared): the ADX preflight now SUCCEEDS — `[adx-preflight] adx-csa-loom-fmezxj: state=Stopped -> paused` then `estate_paused=true` — and the what-if and the apply skipped as designed. The lane still went RED, at a LATER step: the image-tag revert gate refused because loom-unity runs digest sha256:2aac7d64f4f6f51fee5415a9a33ef19ce2e9d56487ea503e562b80878dccac78 while adoption exported the param file's own default `v0.1`, which resolves in the Gov ACR to sha256:db7a7cb5d232431210575bea73572d5cba4d46fb8f091952f215fbbdaa279540. That refusal is correct about the tag and irrelevant on a stood-down run, and issue #4233 gates that step (and the image preflight, the re-pin and the DLZ publish) on the same declaration so a paused run stands down cleanly instead. The unresolved image-tag defect behind it is the #4064 class - adoption not resolving LOOM_UNITY_TAG for the digest-pinned sovereign loom-unity - and is filed separately; nothing here fixes it. WHAT IS NO LONGER ESTABLISHED: the earlier `InsufficientResourcesForSubscription` capacity refusal on the current SKU cannot be observed while this declaration stands, because a declared pause makes the preflight stop attempting the start. It is UNKNOWN whether that capacity condition persists, not resolved. TO RESUME: start the cluster (Gov still has no pause/resume path - scripts/measure/estate-resume.mjs hard-codes the Commercial resource group and a different cluster), confirm it reaches Running, and delete this entry.
paused.$renewedOnBlocked: TRACKED AS ISSUE #4375 — a blocker recorded only inside a data file is on nobody's list, so it is mirrored there too. This entry's fresh read was taken on 2026-09-07 and rule 6 says a renewal records it in `renewedOn`. It is NOT set, and that is a blocker rather than an oversight: scripts/ci/__tests__/estate-preflight.test.mjs:1375 ('the SHIPPED register is structurally valid') classifies every shipped entry with `today: e.declaredOn`, and _estate-pause-declaration.mjs:225 rejects an entry whose `renewedOn` is later than `today`. Since a renewal is BY DEFINITION later than declaredOn, that test rejects every possible renewal — re-measured 2026-09-07 at this head: adding "renewedOn": "2026-09-07" here fails it with "GCC-High's shipped entry is rejected by the classifier" (RC=1, 77 pass / 1 fail), against RC=0 78/78 with the field absent; the file was restored byte-identical afterwards. The field the rule tells you to set cannot be set while that assertion stands. Fixing it means pinning the shipped-entry classification to `renewedOn ?? declaredOn` (or to a fixed today), which is a change to that test file and is out of this change's scope. `reviewBy` is deliberately NOT bumped either: this renewal changed only the recorded observation, not the expiry window, so the lane still re-reds on 2026-11-24 exactly as originally declared.
